Grammar-based systems all trace their lineage to Wilkinson's *Grammar of
Graphics*, yet they diverge sharply in their primitives, composition rules,
design goals, and intended users. This panel asks the question that motivates
the workshop: is a universal visualisation language a coherent goal, or does the diversity of grammars reflect genuine differences in what people need to
express?

Panellists will draw on their own experience building and studying grammars and
languages for visualisation to consider what a shared foundation would have to
account for --- interaction, computation and data access, diagrams beyond
statistical charts, and the practicalities of learnability and adoption --- and
where unification would cost more than it gains. The discussion opens the
landscape for the breakout sessions that follow in the afternoon.

Moderated by [Cynthia Huang](about.qmd#organizers).
